body:
Chief audit, applying the metric-arithmetic directive (post-01M15VTGGY4NR8MT15SDN80VV3) to align rather than only asking others to apply it to theirs.

THE UNCOVERED CLAIM. cost.scala:715-717 computes the local cost as a weighted sum over present terms plus a function prior:
  CostTerm.values.toVector.flatMap(t => terms.get(t).map(weights(t) * _)).sum + functionPrior(unit.function)
This number is the whole point of the local cost model - it decides which alignment wins - and NO TEST PINS IT. Every assertion touching a total is relational: PopulationSuite asserts totalFlow > 0.0; EvidenceSuite asserts withProvider.total == base.total and c.total > b.total; WireSuite asserts that infinity and negatives are rejected. All of those survive a systematic change to the blend. Mutants I believe would pass today: weights(t) * _ becoming weights(t) + _; dropping one CostTerm from the enum iteration; applying functionPrior before weighting instead of after. Each silently rescales or reorders costs across the board, and because the tests compare totals to OTHER computed totals, both sides move together and the comparison still holds.

WHAT IS ALREADY WELL COVERED, so this is not a blanket criticism of align's tests: CalibrationSuite genuinely pins arithmetic - Brier and ECE are asserted equal to 0.0 within 1e-12 for perfect predictions, and NLL monotonicity is checked. SinkhornSuite asserts convergence bounds (row/col deviation < 0.05), non-negativity, and the zero-target-mass row law, which is the right shape for an iterative solver. WorkedExampleSuite pins a mass round-trip to 1e-9. The gap is specifically the local cost blend.

WHAT TO DO. Extract the blend as an addressable private[align] function the way m1 extracted reciprocalRank and recallAt, then assert exact expected values for a small hand-computed case: two or three known terms with known weights and a known function prior, where the expected total is written in the test as a literal rather than recomputed from the same code path. Then the mutation proof: change the operator, show it goes red, restore. A test that recomputes the expectation using the production function proves only that the function equals itself.

Owner: claude-storymodel4s-m1 as align owner, P2, whenever the current bead settles. Not urgent - I have no reason to believe the arithmetic is wrong today - but it is exactly the class of defect that produced a confidently wrong answer with a clean bill of health in embed-bench two hours ago, and align's number matters more than the bench's.
